{{Current events|year=2022|month=01|day=5|content=
<!-- All news items below this line -->
'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[2022 Kazakh protests]]
**A nationwide [[state of emergency]] is declared in [[Kazakhstan]]. [https://news.sky.com/story/kazakhstan-state-of-emergency-declared-in-capital-nur-sultan-as-protests-intensify-in-almaty-and-other-cities-12509441 (Sky News)]
**Eight [[Law enforcement in Kazakhstan|police officers]] are killed and 317 others injured in clashes between protesters and security forces. No figures on civilian casualties have been released. [https://www.reuters.com/world/asia-pacific/eight-police-national-guard-troops-dead-317-injured-during-unrest-kazakhstan-2022-01-05/ (Reuters)]
**The presidential residence and offices of [[Äkim of Almaty]] [[Bakhytzhan Sagintayev]] are set on fire by protesters. [https://apnews.com/article/business-kazakhstan-almaty-9da42330ca51c36fe9fd88f9ef35ff4e (AP)]
**The [[government of Kazakhstan]] [[resign]]s following the protests, with [[Alihan Smaiylov]] becoming acting [[Prime Minister of Kazakhstan|Prime Minister]]. [[President of Kazakhstan|President]] [[Kassym-Jomart Tokayev]] also announces the reintroduction of the [[price cap]] on [[liquefied petroleum gas]]. [https://www.dw.com/en/kazakhstan-government-resigns-following-fuel-price-protests/a-60332403  (Deutsche Welle)]
**President Tokayev dismisses former president and [[Security Council of Kazakhstan]] Chairman [[Nursultan Nazarbayev]]. Protesters also seize control of [[Almaty International Airport]] with all flights to and from the airport being cancelled. [https://www.reuters.com/markets/commodities/kazakhstan-government-resigns-after-violent-protests-over-fuel-price-2022-01-05/ (Reuters)]
**President Tokayev requests military assistance from the [[Collective Security Treaty Organization]], saying that "[[Terrorism and counter-terrorism in Kazakhstan|terrorist]] gangs are overrunning strategic facilities across the country." [https://en.trend.az/casia/kazakhstan/3536865.html (Trend)]
*[[Kivu conflict]]
**Two [[Land Forces of the Democratic Republic of the Congo|soldiers]] and 18 rebels are killed in a clash between [[Banyamulenge]] rebels and government forces in the [[Democratic Republic of the Congo]]. [https://english.alarabiya.net/News/world/2022/01/05/At-least-18-militia-fighters-killed-in-DR-Congo-Army (Al Arabiya)]

'''Arts and culture'''
*[[79th Golden Globe Awards]]
**It is announced that the upcoming [[Golden Globe Awards]] will be held without a live audience or celebrities due to [[COVID-19]] concerns. [https://www.vanityfair.com/hollywood/2022/01/the-golden-globes-plow-forward-without-celebrities-or-a-red-carpet/amp (''Vanity Fair'')]
*[[64th Annual Grammy Awards]]
**The [[Grammy Awards]] is postponed amidst concerns of the [[SARS-CoV-2]] [[Omicron variant]]. [https://www.cnbc.com/amp/2022/01/05/grammy-awards-postponed-indefinitely-due-to-concerns-about-omicron-covid-spread.html (CNBC)]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*[[2022 Philadelphia apartment fire]]
**Twelve people are killed and two others are injured in a fire at a [[terraced housing|row house]] converted into apartments in the [[Fairmount, Philadelphia|Fairmount]] neighborhood of [[Philadelphia]], [[Pennsylvania]], [[United States]]. [https://abcnews.go.com/amp/US/fatal-fire-breaks-philadelphia-row-house/story?id=82086627 (ABC News)]
*Fourteen people are killed and three others are injured by a [[landslide]] at a [[construction]] site in [[Bijie]], [[Guizhou]], [[China]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2022/1/4/several-killed-in-chinese-construction-site-landslide (Al Jazeera)]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Asia]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in India]]
****[[COVID-19 pandemic in Maharashtra]]
*****[[Mumbai]] reports a record 15,166 new cases of [[COVID-19]] in the past 24 hours. [https://www.deccanherald.com/amp/national/west/mumbai-reports-record-15166-new-covid-19-cases-active-cases-above-61000-1068287.html (''Deccan Herald'')]
****[[COVID-19 pandemic in Rajasthan]]
*****[[India]] reports its first confirmed death related to the SARS-CoV-2 Omicron variant in a 73-year-old man who died last week at a hospital in [[Udaipur]], [[Rajasthan]]. [https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/news/india/india-reports-first-death-linked-to-omicron-coronavirus-variant/articleshow/88707986.cms (''The Economic Times'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Israel]]
****[[COVID-19 vaccination in Israel]]
*****[[Israel|Israeli]] [[President of Israel|President]] [[Isaac Herzog]] and his [[First Lady of Israel|First Lady]] [[Michal Herzog]] receive their fourth dose of the COVID-19 vaccine as [[Israel]] launched the second [[booster dose]] vaccination campaign. [https://www.i24news.tv/en/news/coronavirus/1641400331-israel-s-president-isaac-herzog-jabbed-with-4th-vaccine-dose (I24 News)]
****Israel reports a record 11,978 new cases of COVID-19 in the past 24 hours, thereby bringing the nationwide total of confirmed cases to 1,423,289. [https://english.alarabiya.net/coronavirus/2022/01/05/Israel-records-highest-daily-rise-in-COVID-19-infections (Al-Arabiya English)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the Philippines]]
****[[Iloilo City]] reports its first case of the Omicron variant in a 46-year-old man who traveled from [[Kenya]]. [https://www.rappler.com/nation/iloilo-city-confirms-returning-ofw-first-omicron-case/ (Rappler)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Singapore]], [[COVID-19 vaccination in Singapore]]
****[[Singapore|Singaporean]] [[Ministry of Health (Singapore)|Health Minister]] [[Ong Ye Kung]] announces that [[COVID-19 vaccine]] [[booster shot]]s will be mandatory beginning on February 14 in order for people to maintain fully vaccinated status. [https://www.cnbc.com/2022/01/05/singapore-covid-booster-shots-needed-to-maintain-fully-vaccinated-status.html (CNBC)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in South Korea]], [[COVID-19 drug development]]
****[[South Korea]] signs an agreement to buy an additional 400,000 doses of [[Pfizer]]'s [[Paxlovid]] COVID-19 drug. [https://www.channelnewsasia.com/asia/south-korea-agrees-buy-additional-pfizer-covid-19-pills-2416906 (CNA)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Europe]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Italy]]
****[[Italy]] reports a record for the second consecutive day of 189,109 new cases of COVID-19, thereby bringing the nationwide total of confirmed cases to 6,566,947. [https://www.ansa.it/english/news/general_news/2022/01/05/covid-189109-new-cases-231-more-victims_591d04c0-49fa-46a8-bdb4-68307a7c40d3.html (ANSA)]
****The [[Draghi Cabinet]] signs a decree that makes COVID-19 vaccination mandatory for people over the age of 50 years and also mandates that public and private sector workers of this age group need to show proof of [[COVID-19 vaccination|vaccination]] or recovery or face fines of between €600 and €1,500 beginning on February 15. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2022/jan/05/italy-makes-covid-vaccinations-compulsory-for-over-50s (''The Guardian'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in France]]
****[[France]] reports a record for the second consecutive day of 332,252 new cases of COVID-19, which is also the highest daily total recorded in any European nation since the beginning of the pandemic. [https://www.france24.com/en/live-news/20220105-france-reports-new-record-of-more-than-332-000-new-covid-19-cases-in-24-hours (France 24)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the Netherlands]]
****The [[Netherlands]] reports a record 24,590 new cases of COVID-19 in the past 24 hours. [https://nltimes.nl/2022/01/05/new-dutch-covid-record-set-24590-infections-records-amsterdam-rotterdam (NL Times)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Poland]]
****[[Poland|Polish]] [[President of Poland|President]] [[Andrzej Duda]] tests positive for COVID-19 for the second time. He previously tested positive in October 2020. [https://www.voanews.com/a/poland-s-president-tests-positive-for-covid-19-top-aide-says-/6383514.html (Voice of America)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Argentina]]
***[[Argentina]] confirms their first locally transmitted cases of the [[SARS-CoV-2 Omicron variant]]. In response, the [[Government of Argentina|government]] implements self-testing in order to avoid queues at testing centers. [https://www.pagina12.com.ar/393323-la-variante-omicron-ya-tiene-circulacion-comunitaria-en-la-a (''Página/12'')]
***Argentina reports a record for the second consecutive day of 95,159 new cases of COVID-19. [https://www.ambito.com/informacion-general/coronavirus/record-absoluto-casos-covid-19-95159-24-horas-n5347148 (Ámbito)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Australia]]
***[[Australia]] announces [[COVID-19 rapid antigen test|rapid antigen tests]] will be made free to [[Discounts and allowances|concession card]] holders amid a nationwide shortage, but resists calls for universal free access. [https://www.theguardian.com/australia-news/2022/jan/05/coalition-wont-budge-on-free-rapid-covid-tests-for-all-but-concession-card-holders-are-covered (''The Guardian'')]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United States]]
***[[COVID-19 vaccination in the United States]]
****The US [[Centers for Disease Control and Prevention]] (CDC) endorses the use of booster shots of the [[Pfizer–BioNTech COVID-19 vaccine]] for children as young as 12. [https://amp.cnn.com/cnn/2022/01/05/health/cdc-acip-pfizer-covid-vaccine-boosters-adolescents/index.html (CNN)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Illinois]]
****[[Chicago Public Schools]] announces that public schools in [[Chicago]], [[Illinois]], will cancel in-person classes amidst a rise in cases of [[COVID-19]]. [https://abcnews.go.com/amp/US/chicago-cancels-public-school-officials-teachers-reach-impasse/story?id=82086573 (ABC News)]

'''International relations'''
*[[2021 Belarus–European Union border crisis]], [[Belarus–Lithuania relations]]
**The [[Government of Lithuania|Lithuanian government]] announces that it will not extend the state of emergency at [[Belarus–Lithuania border|the border]] with [[Belarus]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/lithuania-will-not-extend-state-emergency-belarus-border-2022-01-05/ (Reuters)]
